What Is a Residential Proxy? IPs, Sessions, and Billing

Understand how residential proxy traffic is routed, when to choose a rotating or fixed exit, and what to check before picking a redrock plan.

A residential proxy forwards a request from your application to a destination. The destination typically sees the public IP of the proxy exit. The address is associated with a residential access network or an ISP. The proxy changes your network route. Your application and the destination still control identity and permissions.

Separate exit network from session length

Residential, mobile, and datacenter describe the type of network carrying the outbound connection. Rotating, sticky, and static describe how long you can keep using the same exit. A regional rendering check may only need a location. A stateful test may depend on both the location and the session.

Choose between rotating and static residential

For authorized checks of page layout, language, or asset loading across regions, group your samples by location and record each exit IP. If several requests must use one exit, check the sticky-session duration available on the rotating plan. If your own service uses a long-lived IP allowlist, evaluate the fixed exit on redrock's static residential plan.

Estimate the workload in the billing unit you will actually use. Traffic matters for rotating residential plans. IP count and term matter for static residential plans. Measure usage, success rate, and latency in a trial, then compare the current plans.

Verify the setup with a small test

Start with a site you have permission to test and record a direct connection as the baseline. Configure the proxy protocol and location, then check the exit IP, response, and session continuity. Repeat a few times and record failures or latency changes.

Continue using TLS and protect your account credentials. Remove temporary credentials when testing ends. Keep proxy passwords out of screenshots, support tickets, and public repositories.

Frequently asked questions

Will a residential IP stay the same indefinitely?

A rotating plan keeps an exit according to its session parameters and terms. For a long-lived fixed exit, review the static residential plan and its renewal conditions.

When should I try a datacenter proxy first?

For an authorized service that needs a stable route without a residential exit, compare datacenter options for cost, latency, and concurrency.
